newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Keppel, Shell invest in LPG plant in Suzhou, China.
newsitem.headline: Keppel, Shell invest in LPG plant in Suzhou, China.

SINGAPORE, May 26 (Reuter) - Keppel Integrated Engineering (KIE) said on Monday it had formed a joint venture with Shell (China) and Suzhou Industrial Shell Park Administration Committee (SIPAC) to build liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) facilities in Suzhou. The joint venture is 20 percent owned by KIE, 45 percent by Shell and 35 percent by SIPAC, the company said in a statement. KIE is a subsidiary of Singapore listed company Keppel Corp Ltd.

The joint venture has invested about US$10 million in an LPG plant which has operated since May 1996 in the China-Singapore Suzhou Industrial Park, the statement said. The plant will operate for 30 years.
The industrial park, which spans 70 sq km, is located in China's Jiangsu province near Shanghai and is supported by Singapore and Chinese companies with backing from their respective governments.
KIE said the joint venture also plans to participate in the manufacture and supply of LPG for phases two and three of the Suzhou Industrial park.
"The gas plant investment follows an earlier agreement when KIE and Shell agreed to jointly develop the LPG business in the lower Yangtze delta," it said.
The plant has started LPG distribution to Phase One of the Suzhou Industrial Park through a comprehensive gas network for piped town gas.
It also provides LPG in cylinders and bulk carriers for commercial and industrial users, it said.
The plant has a generating capacity of 22,400 tonnes a year.
